sections.h2: Which Campbell County offices touch a Northern Kentucky tax bill?
sections.html:
Three offices share a Campbell bill. The Property Valuation Administrator sets the value, the Sheriff's Office mails and collects, and the County Clerk inherits what goes delinquent. Rates come from neither the PVA nor the sheriff: the PVA's page explains that every taxing district's board figures its rate from the assessments inside that district.

The county runs along the Ohio and Licking Rivers and has two seats, Newport and Alexandria, with sheriff's windows in each. At 93,076 residents in 2020 and 615 people per square mile, Campbell is the densest county in this group by a wide margin, and it has the highest home values.

By law the PVA assesses at 100 percent of fair market value, meaning the price a willing buyer and seller would agree on. Field staff look at every parcel in person at least every four years, and new construction is reviewed when it appears.

sections.h2: What is the Campbell County payment calendar?
sections.html:
The PVA's calendar has finished bills reaching the sheriff by September 15, and mailing usually follows around November 1. For 2025 the sheriff ran the discount phase from November 1 through November 30, which the PVA's calendar phrases as payment with discount before December 1.

  • All of December: face amount, no discount.
  • All of January: delinquent, plus 5 percent.
  • From February 1: plus 10 percent and a 10 percent sheriff's add-on fee.
  • Older years: settled at the County Clerk, never the sheriff.

One line item surprises owners: the 911 fee printed on the bill is exempt from the 2% discount and stays at full price. The sheriff mails only to the owner of record and cannot redirect a bill to a lender, so anyone with escrow should pass the bill along at once.

sections.h2: What are the ways to pay in Newport or Alexandria?
sections.html:
Owners can pay online, by mail, or at either sheriff's location. Newport's office sits in the County Administration Building at 1098 Monmouth Street, and Alexandria's is at 8330 West Main Street. The sheriff's tax page lists weekday hours of 8:00 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. for both.

The web option goes through an outside vendor. A card payment adds a 3 percent charge to the cardholder, an e-check adds $3, and e-checks above $30,000 are refused. The sheriff keeps none of those fees. A mailed check should name the sheriff and show the bill number, and the canceled check is your receipt.

A returned check puts the bill back to unpaid on the sheriff's and PVA's records, and the repayment must follow the schedule printed on the bill. That matters in a closing week, when a bounced check can leave a lien open.

sections.h2: How does a Campbell County appeal work?
sections.html:
A PVA conference has to happen before the 13-day inspection period ends, and the appeal itself is filed with the county. Inspection starts the first Monday in May, per the PVA's calendar, and the Board of Assessment Appeals then meets for five days starting 25 to 35 days after it closes.

The state calendar sets the filing deadline at the workday after inspection ends, while the county PVA's calendar lists six work days. With the two sources differing, read the dates on your notice and get the exact last day from the PVA before filing. Anyone paid to represent you must be an attorney, appraiser, accountant, licensed broker or similar professional under KRS 133.120.

Good evidence for a Newport or Alexandria house includes recent sales of similar homes, photos of damage and repair estimates. The state revenue guide adds that the PVA should be able to hand over the sales used to value your home, so request that list first.

sections.h2: Which exemptions and corrections can Campbell County owners request?
sections.html:
Owners who reach 65, or who are totally disabled, can apply for a homestead or disability exemption through the PVA, which can state the filing cutoff for the year. The state wants disability verification before December 31. The sheriff's page advises owners turning 65 to contact the PVA before paying.

The PVA at 1098 Monmouth Street, (859) 292-3871, also fixes a wrong property address, mailing address or owner name. Corrections can be written on the return stub, which the sheriff forwards. An assessment or exemption can be changed only by the PVA.

Farm acreage is valued at its agricultural value, which the state's assessment guide says can sit far below the market price per acre in urban areas. A seller with a few acres at the edge of Alexandria should ask the PVA how the parcel is classed.

sections.h2: What happens to Campbell County taxes when I sell?
sections.html:
The debt travels with the parcel, so the title company will want a payoff of the current bill and any delinquent certificate before closing. KRS 134.015 makes the tax a personal debt of the owner on the January 1 assessment date, and the delinquency lien continues under KRS 134.420 no matter who owns the house afterward.

A bill that outlasts the sheriff's season moves to the County Clerk carrying a 10 percent penalty, the sheriff's fee and 1 percent monthly interest. Clerk, county attorney and third-party purchaser fees pile on from there, and the state's collection page works five examples, running from about $1,388 to $1,704 on a $1,000 bill. The clerk at (859) 292-3845 gives the live figure.

An owner who has fallen behind can still sell as-is, with the payoff deducted from proceeds. Early numbers from the clerk show what remains.

sections.h2: How strong is the Campbell County housing market?
sections.html:
Home values here lead this group: $252,000 is the 2020 to 2024 median for owner-occupied homes, and 182 building permits were issued in 2025. The county belongs to the Cincinnati metropolitan area, and Northern Kentucky University is in Highland Heights.

Only 86.1 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier, the lowest of the four counties, which points to more moves and more rentals. Owners of older Newport homes, duplexes or inherited houses can sell directly for cash when repairs or tenants slow a standard listing.

faqs.q: When do Campbell County tax bills go out?
faqs.a: Mailing typically happens around November 1. In 2025 the 2% discount lasted through November 30, December was face value, January added 5%, and after January 31 a 10% penalty and sheriff's fee applied.

faqs.q: Where do I take a Campbell County payment?
faqs.a: Visit the Sheriff's Office in Newport (1098 Monmouth Street) or Alexandria (8330 West Main Street), mail it, or use the vendor link on the sheriff's tax page.
No. The sheriff states that the 911 line on a bill is outside the 2% discount.

faqs.q: Who handles questions about my Campbell value?
faqs.a: The PVA, at (859) 292-3871. The sheriff only collects, and cannot alter an assessment, address or exemption.

faqs.q: Can a house with unpaid Campbell taxes still sell?
faqs.a: Yes. Delinquent bills sit with the County Clerk, and closing pays them from the proceeds. Ask the clerk, at (859) 292-3845, for the amount before fixing a date.
